category.instructions: Which category best describes this reverted Finnish Wikipedia edit?

criteria.vandalism: Deliberate damage: obscenity, insults, slurs, mockery, jokes, graffiti, or blanking a page or section.
criteria.test_or_nonsense: Keyboard mashing, test edits ('testi'), formatting experiments, or meaningless gibberish with no apparent intent.
criteria.good_faith_error: Seemingly sincere contribution reverted as wrong, unsourced, misplaced, duplicated, or against style rules without an agenda.
criteria.content_dispute: Sincere editorial disagreement over content, emphasis, or wording without a clearly one-sided narrative.
criteria.pov_push: Wording or selection that pushes a political, nationalist, or ideological point of view or narrative via loaded language or one-sided framing.
criteria.false_factual_claim: Asserts or changes a specific checkable fact (number, date, name, place, or causal event) so that it misrepresents the subject.
criteria.source_manipulation: Adds, removes, or alters references, citations, or attributions so that the sourcing misrepresents the content.
criteria.other: None of the content categories above: bot or tool error, technical/template/markup/whitespace change, self-cleanup, link spam, or advertising.
criteria.none_of_these: Cannot be classified into any listed edit category from the provided diff and context.

level.instructions: Which evidence level from the Wikipedia edit-history standard applies to this item?
criteria: Not an incident: non-substantive markup/template/whitespace edit, self-removal, bot edit, page/section blanking, kept in the latest article, or obvious vandalism/test graffiti.
Removed by Wikipedia editors: substantive content added and later removed by a different editor, without both a disputed claim and a community dispute over accuracy, neutrality, or sourcing.

Disputed and removed: a factual claim, POV push, content dispute, or source manipulation that another editor disputed over accuracy, neutrality, or sourcing, or that was re-inserted or part of an edit war.
Pattern consistent with a coordinated attempt: a disputed claim pushed by multiple editors or across multiple articles, or repeatedly re-inserted over at least 7 days alongside source manipulation.
